channel.description: Latest articles from Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) – Bias and Credibility (ppic.org)

item.title: Commentary: Why Civic Education Matters Now More than Ever
item.description: The second week of March is known as Civic Learning Week, an effort to promote the importance of understanding our governing system. In a time of deep political polarization, the need is urgent.

item.title: How Are California’s Young Adults Faring Economically?
item.description: Unemployment is currently higher among California’s young adults than others. But rates of disconnection from both work and school are improving—with variation across the state.

item.title: Chronic Absenteeism in California
item.description: Missing school for 18 days or more is linked to academic underachievement, and any student absences affect districts, as school funding is based on attendance. Statewide, chronic absenteeism has dropped from its peak but remains well above rates before the pandemic; furthermore, improvement has slowed in the last year.

item.title: Celebrating Fish Biologist Peter Moyle
item.description: UC Davis professor emeritus Peter Moyle is arguably the most important fish biologist in California’s history. Last Saturday, a stellar collection of California water leaders, agency heads, wildlife experts, and Moyle’s students and family gathered to pay homage to the man behind the mustache.

item.title: New Salton Sea Research Suggests a Surprising Path Forward
item.description: Managing the Salton Sea remains a thorny issue for California. We spoke with Pacific Institute’s Michael Cohen and UC Riverside’s William Porter about recent research that might point toward cost-effective ways to protect public health in the region.

item.title: Public Health Insurance in California
item.description: Public health insurance covers about half of Californians, including low- to moderate-income, older, and disabled individuals, as well as military members and veterans.

item.title: California’s Health Care Safety Net
item.description: Medi-Cal is a cornerstone of California’s health care safety net, insuring over 14 million low-income Californians, and is a key funding source for core safety net providers.

item.title: Most Californians Expect Little Change to Their Finances Despite Economic Uncertainty
item.description: An overwhelming majority of Californians see bad financial times ahead and don’t think their income is keeping up with inflation. Still, most expect their own finances to hold steady—for now.

item.title: California’s Water Agencies Begin Looking to AI
item.description: As pressure grows for workers to use AI, most California water agencies are just beginning to take advantage of the technology. How are water agencies currently using AI, and what should they consider as they adopt it? We spoke with experts who shared some key first steps.

item.title: California’s K–12 Test Scores
item.description: In 2025, half of California’s K–12 students met the state standard in English, while a third did so in math. Although proficiency rates have improved in recent years, scores remain lower than before the pandemic and longstanding achievement gaps persist among demographic groups.
